answer: Operator-Linked Identity Ledger. Each new identity must be anchored to a hardware root that is cross-checked against an operator-owned directory; duplicate roots collapse to one vertex. If a cluster of identities shares a root, the operator loses a fixed saffron credit line per duplicate, charged against their infrastructure lease. To scale, an attacker must acquire distinct roots at full price plus the credit penalty on every collision, pushing marginal cost from near-zero to thousands per identity.
